title: Optimize walkthrough - quant profiles (INT8/FP8) - Veridian Analytics
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focusing on INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles. Covered quality vs latency tradeoffs, sample benchmarks on Veridian-like LLM workloads, suggested profiles for low-latency inference and best-effort quality retention. Customer asked about drift in QA prompts, SLOs for 99th pct latency, and how rollback/rollouts work for quantized variants.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we have about 50 minutes, uh we'll run through our Optimize flow for quant profiles — INT8 and FP8 — and then look at some sample benchmarks and recommended profiles for your summarization and search use cases.
[00:12] Carlos Mendoza: yeah thanks Liam, excited, we had a quick internal note, we run batch summaries and a real-time chat assistant; latency is important for chat but cost for batch is huge so we're trying to understand tradeoffs.
[00:25] Riya Kapoor: quick intro, I'm Riya on the SE side, I'll share my screen in a sec, show the console and the optimize tab, and point to where we store quant profiles.
[00:35] Priya Shah: cool, also, uh our models are a mix of open LLMs and a couple custom fine-tuned variants, anything special for fine-tuned weights?
[00:44] Riya Kapoor: good question. For fine-tuned variants we usually generate a profile using our profiling job — it collects activation distributions and suggests per-layer quant parameters; works for both INT8 and FP8. sometimes names are a bit off in the auto transcript, sorry if it's messy.
[00:58] [01:00] Riya Kapoor (screen): so here on the Optimize tab you can see quant profiles, each profile has policy buckets: latency-slim, balanced, quality-first. we recommend starting with "balanced" for production and testing latency-slim in a canary.
[01:15] Ethan Li: can you share specific numbers? like p99 latency change when moving from fp16 to int8 or fp8?
[01:23] Riya Kapoor: sure so these are approximate from our internal runs on A100s and some T4-like configs: fp16 baseline p99 for a 512-token request ~ 420ms, INT8 balanced ~ 320ms, INT8 latency-slim ~ 260ms, FP8 balanced ~ 290ms. quality-wise we see ROUGE/Exact-match drops in the 0.5-1.5% range for balanced INT8 on generative summarization, and smaller drops with FP8 depending on ops.
[01:48] Priya Shah: 0.5-1.5% is okay for most of our summaries, but for legal doc extraction accuracy needs to be higher, would you recommend FP8 there?
[01:58] Riya Kapoor: for high-stakes extraction we usually recommend FP8 or a mixed strategy: keep the critical extraction model in fp16 or fp32 and use INT8 for less-critical LLM paths. Also Redwood supports per-route quant overrides in the console so you can route specific endpoints to different profiles.
[02:15] [02:20] Liam Chen: another option is auto-fallback — if the quantized variant fails quality checks on rolling sample prompts, traffic falls back to the baseline model automatically. it helps with gradual rollouts.
[02:34] Carlos Mendoza: what's the overhead to run the profiling job? like time/cost?
[02:39] Riya Kapoor: profiling typically runs in 10-30 minutes for a 1000-sample dataset; cost is small relative to full evals, we provide a one-click profile in the console. we snapshot KV cache behaviour too so the runtime can pick appropriate kernels.
[02:55] Priya Shah: how do you measure "quality" automatically? we have a custom eval set and human-in-the-loop checks — can we plug that in?
[03:04] Riya Kapoor: yes you can upload your eval prompts, Redwood Optimize will compute metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Exact) and compare across profiles. you can also wire our regression alerts to Slack or email.
[03:15] Maya Ortiz: can you show the spreadsheet you mentioned with the latency vs quality curve?
[03:20] Riya Kapoor: sure, link in the deck — "benchmark spreadsheet" — I'll drop it to the chat after the call. sample numbers we looked at: for your summarization workload, switching to INT8 balanced saved ~34% token cost, FP8 saved ~28% but with slightly better quality retention in structured extraction tasks.
[03:38] [03:45] Priya Shah: are there known failure modes? like hallucinations increase with INT8?
[03:50] Riya Kapoor: sometimes you see small degradations in long-form coherence; hallucination risk depends more on prompt framing and temperature but quantization can amplify edge-case behaviours. that's why we suggest AB tests and a canary with auto-rollbacks.
[04:07] Ethan Li: from infra side, for our private deployment (VPC) — does profiling run in our cluster or is it on Redwood infra?
[04:14] Riya Kapoor: for Private deployments profiling can run inside your VPC if you enable that option; for Redwood-hosted we run it in our secure sandbox. we also provide KMS integration for keys and do not persist raw customer data beyond the profiling period unless you opt-in.
[04:32] Carlos Mendoza: security docs — can you share SOC2 and a short note on audit logs for quant profiles?
[04:37] Liam Chen: yes, we'll share the security pack, and note in the console audit logs include profile creation, rollout changes, and who approved canary promotions.
[04:47] [04:50] Riya Kapoor: demo time — I'm going to create a new profile from your sample eval. selecting model variant "veridian-summarize-v1" (we had a small name mismatch due to transcription), choosing 1000-sample eval, run profile.
[05:05] Riya Kapoor: profiling output: per-layer scale factors, suggested per-op clipping, and overall expected token quant error. it also outputs a quality delta estimate vs baseline.
[05:18] Priya Shah: you mentioned mixed precision — how do you actually configure that?
[05:21] Riya Kapoor: in the profile you get a dropdown, choose mixed-int8-fp8 and you can map certain operation types or layers to fp8. we also expose a manual override for sensitive layers.
[05:34] [05:40] Liam Chen: let's talk timeline — if you want to run a pilot, typical flow: share evals and infra access (if private), run profiling and benching (1-2 days), canary with 5-10% traffic for 1 week, then ramp.
[05:52] Carlos Mendoza: budget-wise what should we expect for the bench runs?
[05:56] Liam Chen: bench runs are modest; profiling + a couple of bench suites maybe a few hundred dollars on hosted; major cost savings come post-conversion from reduced token and GPU time. we can share a sample cost model spreadsheet.
[06:09] [06:15] Priya Shah: on rollback — if we see a quality regression after ramp, is rollback instantaneous?
[06:19] Riya Kapoor: yes, we support immediate rollback to previous model/profile at routing layer, plus automatic fallback per-request; you can also set a health policy so traffic is diverted if p99 exceeds threshold.
[06:32] Maya Ortiz: what's the relation between batching size and quant gains?
[06:36] Riya Kapoor: batching improves GPU utilization but latency interplay matters; INT8 often allows higher batch sizes because memory footprint drops, which improves throughput and unit-cost, but you should test because p99 might increase if batching waits for tokens. our Optimize tool models batch/latency tradeoffs in the profile results.
[06:55] [07:00] Carlos Mendoza: any gotchas with serving runtimes — like kernel availability for FP8 on older cards?
[07:06] Riya Kapoor: yes FP8 kernel support varies by backend; we detect compatible kernels and may fall back to emulation which hurts perf. we'll flag kernels incompatibility in the profile and recommend a compatible infra plan or an INT8 fallback.
[07:20] Priya Shah: question on eval sensitivity — can we threshold on multiple metrics? like exact-match > 97% and rouge > x?
[07:26] Riya Kapoor: absolutely, you can define composite thresholds and Redwood will surface violations during canary and block promotion if thresholds fail.
[07:36] [07:40] Liam Chen: quick competitor note: a few vendors only do end-to-end quantization without per-layer tuning, that's why our per-layer profiling tends to retain more quality.
[07:50] Ethan Li: ok, runbook — in our runbooks we want a checklist for production rollouts, can you share that?
[07:55] Liam Chen: yes we have a "production rollouts" checklist — I'll attach to the CRM and share after call.
[08:03] [08:10] Riya Kapoor: final demo snippet: launching a canary, setting traffic 10%, setting composite metric thresholds, enabling auto-fallback. launching... canary active.
[08:22] Priya Shah: awesome, that UI looks good.
[08:25] Carlos Mendoza: last Q — if we want to keep model in Dedicated or Private, does the Optimize tooling still work?
[08:31] Riya Kapoor: yes it's same API and console; for Dedicated we can schedule profiling on your reserved capacity and integrate with your autoscaling policies. for Private it runs via the private control plane.
[08:43] Liam Chen: ok, time check — about 7 minutes left, let's capture next steps.
[08:48] [08:50] Carlos Mendoza: next steps from our side: share a subset of 1k eval prompts, get infra contact to coordinate VPC access, budget check.
[08:58] Liam Chen: from Redwood: we'll send security docs, sample cost model, benchmark spreadsheet, and a pilot proposal with timeline. we'll also add the production rollout checklist to the CRM deal.
[09:12] Priya Shah: can we get a sample mixed profile recommended for our extraction route?
[09:16] Riya Kapoor: yes we'll generate a recommended mixed profile and attach it to the pilot artifacts.
[09:22] [09:25] Liam Chen: wrap up — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with email and calendar invite for a pilot kickoff.
[09:30] Carlos Mendoza: thanks, bye.

Customer to share 1k eval prompts and provide infra contact for VPC access
Redwood to upload benchmark spreadsheet and sample cost model
Redwood to generate recommended mixed INT8/FP8 profile for extraction route
